title: Senior Recruiter
description: Wij zoeken geen recruiter die wacht op sollicitaties. adesso Nederland groeit. En de mensen die wij zoeken, zijn meestal niet actief op zoek naar een nieuwe baan. Daarom zoeken we een Senior Recruiter die recruitment écht beheerst. Iemand die begrijpt dat een vacature online zetten het begin is en niet de strategie. Je weet hoe je zelf de markt in gaat. Je searcht, sourcet, benadert en bouwt relaties op. Je probeert verschillende invalshoeken als een search niet werkt. Je kent LinkedIn Recruiter, maar weet ook dat sourcing meer is dan een paar zoektermen invoeren en InMails versturen. En misschien nog belangrijker: je hebt ideeën. Over waar we talent kunnen vinden. Over hoe we mensen kunnen benaderen. Over employer branding. Over onze propositie als werkgever. Over tooling, data, events, referrals, communities en alles wat ons kan helpen om betere mensen aan adesso te verbinden. Zie je een kans? Dan verwachten we niet dat je wacht tot iemand je vertelt wat je moet doen. Je pakt hem. Wat ga je doen? Je krijgt verantwoordelijkheid voor recruitment binnen adesso Nederland en werkt nauw samen met hiring managers en management. Daarbij ben je zowel strategisch als operationeel. Want senior zijn betekent bij ons niet dat je alleen adviseert. Je doet het ook zelf. Je: voert zelfstandig searches uit naar schaarse IT-professionals; bouwt talentpools op in plaats van pas te zoeken zodra er een vacature ontstaat; benadert kandidaten persoonlijk en weet hun interesse te wekken; experimenteert met nieuwe sourcingkanalen en manieren van benaderen; voert intakes met hiring managers en durft kritisch te zijn op het profiel dat zij zoeken; adviseert over haalbaarheid, arbeidsmarkt, salaris en recruitmentstrategie; voert gesprekken met kandidaten en begeleidt het proces van eerste contact tot hire; houdt overzicht over je vacatures en neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor het resultaat; gebruikt data om te begrijpen wat wel en niet werkt; komt zelf met voorstellen om recruitment slimmer en effectiever te maken; denkt mee over employer branding, referral recruitment, events en communities; bouwt mee aan hoe recruitment binnen adesso Nederland zich verder ontwikkelt. Je krijgt daarbij geen dichtgetimmerd recruitmenthandboek. We verwachten juist dat jij vanuit je ervaring kunt zeggen: “Dit werkt niet. Ik denk dat we het zo moeten aanpakken.” En vervolgens help je om het te realiseren. Wanneer ben je voor ons senior? Niet omdat er ‘Senior Recruiter’ op je LinkedIn-profiel staat. Voor ons zit senioriteit in hoe je werkt. Je hoeft niet gevraagd te worden om te sourcen je weet dat het onderdeel van je vak is. Als een search niets oplevert, concludeer je niet dat “de markt lastig is”. Je verandert je aanpak. Als een hiring manager een onrealistisch profiel zoekt, durf je dat gesprek te voeren. Als je ziet dat ons recruitmentproces beter kan, kom je niet alleen met het probleem maar ook met een voorstel. En als je een goed idee hebt, krijg je energie van het daadwerkelijk uitvoeren ervan. We zoeken iemand met stevige recruitmentervaring, bij voorkeur binnen IT, tech of consultancy. Maar het aantal jaren ervaring vinden we minder belangrijk dan wat je daadwerkelijk kunt. We willen vooral zien dat je: aantoonbaar sterk bent in search, sourcing en direct benaderen; weet hoe je schaarse senior professionals vindt en interesseert; verschillende sourcingstrategieën kunt bedenken én uitvoeren; creatief bent in het vinden van nieuwe kandidaten en doelgroepen; verantwoordelijkheid neemt voor je vacatures en resultaten; zelfstandig prioriteiten stelt; hiring managers als volwaardig gesprekspartner adviseert; kritisch durft te zijn wanneer dat nodig is; nieuwsgierig bent naar nieuwe recruitmenttechnieken, tooling en AI; met data naar je eigen recruitmentfunnel kijkt; ideeën niet alleen bedenkt, maar ook uitvoert; Nederlands en Engels professioneel beheerst. Wat je bij ons niet hoeft te doen Wachten tot iemand je vertelt welke Boolean search je moet gebruiken. Wachten tot marketing met een employer-brandingidee komt. Wachten tot een hiring manager vraagt waarom een vacature al zes weken openstaat. Of iedere week uitleggen dat de markt nu eenmaal moeilijk is. Natuurlijk is de IT-arbeidsmarkt moeilijk. Dat is precies waarom we een goede Senior Recruiter zoeken. Wat krijg je daarvoor terug? Veel vrijheid. Maar vrijheid betekent bij ons ook verantwoordelijkheid. Je krijgt de ruimte om recruitment mede vorm te geven en nieuwe dingen uit te proberen. adesso werkt met korte lijnen, veel autonomie en ruimte voor initiatief. Onze Culture Code draait onder andere om hands-on, straightforward en open-minded werken . Dat betekent: aanpakken, zeggen wat je denkt en openstaan voor betere ideeën. Verder kun je rekenen op: een vast dienstverband voor 32–40 uur per week; 27 vakantiedagen; 4 studiedagen per jaar; €3.600 persoonlijk ontwikkelbudget per jaar; een mobiliteitsregeling; hybride werken en flexibele werktijden; een goede pensioenregeling en aanvullende verzekeringen; internationale ontwikkelmogelijkheden binnen adesso; en vooral: ruimte om recruitment beter neer te zetten. Klinkt dit bekend? Misschien zie je tijdens het lezen van deze vacature al drie dingen die je anders zou doen. Mooi. Dan zijn we waarschijnlijk naar jou op zoek. We zoeken geen recruiter die onze huidige manier van werken netjes in stand houdt. We zoeken iemand die helpt om hem beter te maken. Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

Maar we verwachten niet dat je alles al hebt gedaan. · Microsoft Fabric; · Azure Databricks; · Azure Data Factory; · Snowflake; · Apache Spark / PySpark; · Delta Lake; · Power BI; · Collibra of andere data governance-oplossingen; · Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry of andere AI-services binnen Azure; · Infrastructure as Code, bijvoorbeeld Terraform of Bicep. Data & AI bij adesso Data is bij ons geen losstaand onderdeel van een project. Het is steeds vaker de basis waarop nieuwe digitale oplossingen worden gebouwd. Van moderne dataplatformen en machine learning tot generative AI en agentic AI: we willen technologie niet alleen interessant vinden, maar vooral werkend krijgen bij onze klanten. raw.title: IoT Embedded Systems Engineer
raw.description:
• Take ownership of the development of IoT systems, with a focus on embedded software, system architecture, and hardware and firmware integration

  • Design and develop robust, efficient, and scalable embedded software for IoT products based on microcontroller platforms and, optionally, Linux based systems

  • Provide technical guidance for hardware development in collaboration with external partners, including reviewing and challenging PCB designs to ensure functionality, quality, and manufacturability

  • Collaborate closely with mechanical, software, and cloud engineering teams to ensure seamless end to end system integration

  • Define and refine product requirements from initial concept through to mass production in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders

  • Develop and integrate prototypes and support the transition from development into serial production together with manufacturing partners

  • Contribute to the continuous evolution of the embedded platform, including MCU based solutions as well as optional Linux and Yocto based components

  • Develop pragmatic testing strategies to ensure the functionality, reliability, and quality of both hardware and firmware

  • Support development and manufacturing partners with debugging, technical documentation, and production ramp up

  • Provide Level 3 technical support for complex system, firmware, and hardware related issues

  • Travel approximately 5 to 10 percent to support development partners, product validation activities, and product launches


  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience

  • Several years of hands on experience in embedded development, including firmware development and hardware related engineering

  • Strong understanding of hardware design and PCB layouts, with the ability to review design decisions and collaborate effectively with hardware development teams

  • Strong expertise in embedded firmware development and software architecture for microcontroller platforms such as ARM Cortex, ESP32, or STM32

  • Experience with sensor integration and wireless communication technologies such as BLE and WiFi

  • Experience with embedded Linux systems, particularly Yocto, is an advantage, especially in environments combining System on Modules with MCU based architectures

  • Broad system level understanding of mechanics, sensors, actuators, and their integration into robust IoT products

  • Hands on experience with hardware testing, debugging tools, and automated production testing

  • Familiarity with certification standards such as CE and FCC is an advantage

  • Fluent in German and English, with additional languages considered a plus

The monorepo covers the full path from experimentation to product: dataset and sample definitions, training and evaluation code, experiment tracking, model export, and the inference servers that run in production. Everyone on the team contributes to the monorepo; this role is the single point of accountability for it. This hands-on role owns the architecture, tooling, and engineering standards of that codebase for a distributed team of about twenty machine learning engineers and scientists, working with model developers and software engineers to make the team’s work fast, better, and easier to audit. It also leads the team's agentic coding strategy, shaping how AI coding agents are used across the codebase. The role reports to the Leader of the ML for X-ray/CT/MRI group. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Own the architecture and roadmap of the ML Monorepo: Module boundaries, shared abstractions for datasets and samples, training and evaluation loops, configuration, and experiment tracking. Build and run the engineering tooling around the codebase: Continuous integration, testing, dependency management, containers, artifact and model registries, and GPU job scheduling on cloud (GCP) and HPC infrastructure. Own the path from trained checkpoint to deployable model: Model packaging, inference servers with enforced API contracts, reproducibility, and performance and memory budgets on target hardware. Define and enforce engineering standards (code review, testing, documentation) in a way that accelerates research rather than slowing it down. Ensure traceability of data, code, and model versions across experiments and releases. Investigate and resolve performance, reliability, and usability issues in the stack raised by the team and reduce their recurrence through shared tooling. Drive the team's agentic coding strategy: define how AI coding agents are used in the monorepo, set up the tooling, guardrails, and conventions that make them effective, and help colleagues adopt them. Review code, mentor colleagues on engineering practices, and communicate technical decisions and trade-offs clearly. Solid PyTorch knowledge and practical experience with model training and profiling (required). Experience running ML workloads on a cloud platform, ideally GCP (Vertex AI, Artifact Registry, IAM, storage), and with containerization (required). Experience taking models to production: model packaging, inference serving, and performance and reliability constraints (required). Ability to work closely with researchers, translate recurring pain points into shared tooling, and push back constructively when needed (required). Ability to work autonomously in a distributed, multi-site team, with clear verbal and written communication in English (required). Medical imaging experience (DICOM, 3D volumes, large images) (preferred). HPC and Slurm experience (preferred). Contributions to open-source ML tooling (preferred). title: Senior Scientific Software Engineer — Simulation and Machine Learning
description:
Location: Remote within Europe, with regular presence in Bremen

Direct Reports: None; supervision of students and interns

Working Model: Remote / hybrid. Regular time on-site in Bremen.

Mission

Build the simulation and model-learning engine at the centre of Constructor's quantum software. The work is numerics-heavy: differentiable simulation of physical systems, inference of model parameters from experimental data, and optimisation at scale. The role sits between physics and engineering and requires genuine depth in both.

Responsibilities

Pillar 1 Simulation Engine

  • Build and maintain high-performance simulation code for open and closed quantum systems.
  • Own the differentiable simulation and automatic differentiation layer.
  • Drive performance. This code runs inside optimisation loops and speed decides what is possible.
  • Maintain and extend the Julia core and its Python interface.

Success Metrics and KPIs: simulation accuracy against measurement, runtime performance, API stability.

Pillar 2 Model Learning and Optimisation

  • Implement parameter inference and model learning from experimental data.
  • Work on neural-network approaches to PDE solving and equation discovery.
  • Benchmark against established academic tools and publish the comparison.

Success Metrics and KPIs: benchmark results, methods adopted by the research group, publications.

Pillar 3 Research Collaboration

  • Work with Constructor University faculty on joint research and grant applications.
  • Supervise graduate students and interns working on the engine.
  • Contribute to course material on numerical simulation and machine learning for physics.

Accountability: research collaborations initiated and sustained; students productive.

Requirements

Experience

  • PhD or equivalent in physics, applied mathematics or computational science.
  • Strong scientific computing in Julia, Python, JAX or comparable.
  • Real numerical depth: ODE solvers, optimisation, stochastic processes, automatic differentiation.
  • Published work, or code that others rely on.

Skills & Competencies

  • Able to take a method from a paper and make it fast, tested and usable.
  • Comfortable owning code quality, not only correctness.
  • Interest in supervising students alongside the engineering.
  • Clear technical writing.

Education & Languages

  • PhD in physics, applied mathematics or computational science.
  • Fluent English.

What This Role Is (and Is Not)

This role IS

  • A research-grade engineering role with a product at the end of it.
  • Central to the group's core technical asset.
  • A role with a route into teaching and supervision if you want it.

This role is NOT

  • A pure research position without delivery.
  • A general software engineering role.
  • A role where someone else owns the numerics.

title: Sales & Client Engagement Director (EMEA + DACH)
description:
About us

Constructor Labs is the research arm of Constructor Knowledge, based at Campus Ring 1 in Bremen, Germany. Our work is organized around three units: Knowledge Labs, Cyber Labs and Science Labs. We apply computing, software and robotics research to make scientists, teachers and students more effective, working with institutional partners that include CERN, NUS, Carnegie Mellon and Fraunhofer.

Our EdTech practice produces research that runs in production. AI-supported remote proctoring is in use at the Irish Aviation Authority, Princess Nourah University and Saudi Electronic University, and our course delivery platform is used by CERN, EPFL, MariaDB and Acronis. For industry clients, we build tailored BSc, MSc and PhD pipelines, L&D operating models, AI upskilling programmes and customer training systems.

Constructor Labs Solutions (CLS) is our client-facing systems integrator for the education and research sector, launching in September 2026. It brings audit and consultancy, content, platform, talent and R&D services together under a single contract, an offer few providers make to education buyers today. Delivery is orchestrated across several Constructor organizations: CUB, Nexford, Nexademy, EBAC, Constructor Labs and Constructor Tech. Our aim is to become the go-to systems integrator for education in EMEA by 2029.

The role

You will open EMEA markets for Constructor Labs Solutions as a quota-carrying individual contributor. The role rests on an established network among universities, online education providers, EdTech vendors and corporate L&D and research buyers, and on your ability to convert that network into signed engagements.

You will work with the marketing and delivery teams to build pipeline, establish the CLS brand and develop a case-study library. Supporting you are a credible research institution, named production references, an existing Constructor and Constructor Tech client base, and delivery capability across five service lines that can be combined into a single proposal.

The sales motion is consultative. Engagements typically open with a low-risk paid diagnostic (Technology Landscape Assessment, Curriculum Gap Analysis or Learning Strategy Advisory), which you then convert into a multi-line implementation or managed-service mandate. Initial engagements start at around €150–250K in lifetime value and grow from there. Sales cycles in public higher education run six to twelve months, so you will manage a long-cycle institutional funnel alongside faster corporate L&D deals.

Reporting and scope

  • Reports to: Director of Sales & Marketing, Constructor Labs Solutions (shared with the Constructor Labs GM during Phase 1).
  • Level: Director, individual contributor. You will join an established sales team.
  • Territory: EMEA, with initial focus on DACH (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) and the UK and Ireland. Named accounts agreed quarterly.
  • Segments: traditional and online universities, EdTech providers and platform vendors, corporate L&D and corporate academies, research-intensive organizations, and publicly funded research programmes.
  • Portfolio: all five CLS service lines, namely Audit & Consultancy, Content, Platform, Talent and R&D Services.

Day-to-day, you will work with the Audit & Consultancy Practice Head on scoping, with Nexademy on content propositions, with Constructor Tech on platform architecture, and with the Labs' principal investigators, who join client conversations to provide subject-matter credibility. Knowing which expert belongs in which conversation is central to the role.

What you will do

  • Pipeline generation. Around 70% of your time is spent on outbound activity: your own network, conference presence, sector associations, procurement frameworks and targeted account campaigns, supported by marketing.
  • Reference accounts. Sign the first reference clients in EMEA and develop each one into a published case study, an active sponsor and a source of introductions.
  • Discovery and scoping. Map the client's learning or research operating model and quantify the problem in their own measures: cost per course, time to accreditation, completion rates, time-to-hire, research throughput. Shape a diagnostic that leads to a defined follow-on engagement.
  • Conversion to implementation. Own the transition from paid diagnostic to multi-line mandate, with a target of converting half of all audit engagements.
  • Proposals and bids. Assemble proposals across the five service lines with the practice heads, price them against the finance model and qualify them against margin floors. Lead RFP and framework responses, including public-sector tenders in Germany and the UK.
  • Stakeholder coverage. Engage rectors, deans, CIOs, heads of digital learning, procurement, works councils, CLOs, HR directors and research directors. Maintain at least three engaged contacts on every opportunity above €200K.
  • Partner channel. Recruit and manage regional partners, resellers, agencies and academic networks that extend reach beyond your direct coverage.
  • Quota and forecasting. You carry an annual new-business quota, with quarterly KPIs covering pipeline coverage, audit conversion, average engagement value and blended margin. Maintain weekly pipeline hygiene in the CRM, submit a forecast you can defend, and flag slippage as soon as you see it.
  • Market feedback. Report what EMEA buyers procure and what they decline, and how our pricing compares with Instructure, D2L, Cornerstone and the generalist integrators, so that the service catalogue can be adjusted.
  • External representation. Speak at sector events and contribute to thought leadership alongside our principal investigators, building recognition for CLS among education buyers in your region.

Targets and KPIs

The role carries a quota set on net-new signed bookings (total contract value) in your territory, with a six-month ramp and a quarterly review:

  • Net-new signed bookings (TCV)
  • Reference clients signed
  • Average engagement value
  • Audit-to-implementation conversion
  • Blended gross margin on signed work
  • New qualified opportunities created
  • Forecast accuracy

What you bring

  • Network in the sector. Eight or more years selling into education, research or corporate learning in EMEA, preferably DACH and/or the UK, with decision-maker relationships you can open within the first 90 days. You should be prepared to discuss your top 15 target accounts and the route into each.
  • A closing record in complex services. Consistent achievement against a quota of €1M or more in professional services, consulting, systems integration or enterprise EdTech, covering six-figure deals, multi-stakeholder buying groups and six- to twelve-month cycles.
  • Consultative selling. Experience selling scoped engagements whose deliverables were defined jointly with the client, and fluency in a recognized methodology such as MEDDIC, Challenger or Command of the Message.
  • Domain credibility. The ability to hold a substantive conversation with a pro-vice-chancellor about digitalization, a CLO about competency frameworks or a research director about co-funded projects, together with a working understanding of how universities and research organizations buy: budget cycles, committee approval, procurement frameworks and public tender rules.
  • Comfort in an early-stage unit. Experience building a territory or a new offering from a standing start, and the ability to sell a service catalogue that is still being completed.
  • Languages. Business-fluent German and English. Both are required, since public education buyers in DACH contract in German.
  • Commercial discipline. Rigorous CRM and forecasting practice, and a readiness to qualify out early rather than carry unlikely deals.
  • Professional integrity. You will represent a research institution to universities and public bodies, so commitments made during the sales process must be ones delivery can meet.

Nice to have

  • Experience selling into publicly funded research programmes, or EU and national grant-co-funded projects (Horizon Europe, Innovate UK, BMBF).
  • Working knowledge of the LMS/SIS landscape and its incumbents — Instructure, D2L, Cornerstone, Moodle, SAP SuccessFactors.
  • Experience with UK public procurement frameworks (Crown Commercial Service, JISC) or German public tendering (VgV, e-Vergabe).
  • Background in the education practice of a systems integrator, Big Four firm or consultancy.
  • Prior success selling talent, recruitment or academic content services.
  • French, Italian or Dutch as a third language.
  • An existing speaking profile in the education or L&D community.

Location and travel

Candidates must be based in Europe and hold an existing, unrestricted right to work in their country of residence. Relocation is not offered for this position: the network the role depends on should already be in the market.

Preferred bases are Germany, Switzerland, Bulgaria or the UK. The role is remote or hybrid, with regular time in Bremen and at the London commercial hub. Expect travel of up to 40% within EMEA for client meetings, tenders and sector events, plus occasional travel to other Constructor locations.

What we offer

  • Base salary and commission, weighted approximately 60/40 at on-target earnings, with accelerators above 100% of quota. The band is competitive for a Director-level individual contributor in DACH or the UK and depends on location and experience.
  • A guaranteed ramp across the first two quarters while the pipeline is built.
  • Commission on margin as well as revenue, so that well-scoped work is rewarded ahead of discounted work.
  • Access to our researchers, including principal investigators, CERN-level data scientists, and education methodologists who will join your client meetings.
  • An existing reference base, including named proctoring and platform deployments.
  • Influence over the offering. As the key commercial voice in these markets, you will shape a service catalogue that is not yet fixed.

Own the architecture of the software platform on which Constructor Labs' quantum group builds. The platform drives physical quantum hardware end to end — calibration, orchestration, experiment execution and device state — and must work both in our own cloud and on customer premises, including restricted and air-gapped environments. The Principal Architect sets the technical direction, makes the structural decisions, and is the senior engineering voice in a group where research and engineering sit closely together.

Responsibilities

Pillar 1 Platform Architecture

  • Own the end-to-end architecture across backend services, job orchestration, hardware abstraction and device state management.
  • Define the interfaces between the scientific layer and the platform layer so physicists can work without engineering support.
  • Make and carry the build-versus-buy and framework decisions; document them so they survive the people who made them.
  • Lead the migration of the platform onto the Constructor technology stack.

Success Metrics and KPIs: architectural decisions documented and adopted, platform stability, migration delivered to plan.

Pillar 2 Hands-on Engineering

  • Write production code in the core of the system, not only design documents.

Success Metrics and KPIs: test coverage, review discipline, bus factor above one on every core component.

Pillar 3 Working with Research

  • Work day to day with research physicists, translating experimental workflows into software.
  • Keep the research and engineering collaboration model intact as the group grows.
  • Support the product function with realistic estimates and honest technical constraints.

Accountability: research team able to run experiments without engineering bottlenecks.

Requirements

Experience

  • 10+ years building production software systems, with real depth in Python, C#/.NET or C++.
  • Distributed systems, job scheduling, and interfacing with instruments or physical hardware.
  • Track record as the senior technical voice in a small team.
  • Delivered software into on-premise and restricted environments, not only cloud.

Skills & Competencies

  • Able to hold an architecture in your head and explain it simply to people who are not engineers.
  • Comfortable in a scientific domain. A physics degree is not required, genuine interest is.
  • Pragmatic about trade-offs; able to ship rather than perfect.
  • Strong written communication. Decisions that are not written down do not exist.

Education & Languages

  • Degree in computer science, physics, engineering or equivalent practical track record.
  • Fluent English. German useful, not required.

What This Role Is (and Is Not)

This role IS

  • Deeply hands-on, with real authority over technical direction.
  • Central to everything the quantum group builds.

title: PhD Position: World Models for Software Architecture Synthesis (Constructor Fabric)
description:
Supervisor: Prof. Dr. Alexander Tormasov

About the Position

Constructor Knowledge Labs (CKL), in collaboration with Constructor Technology, invites applications for a PhD position in machine learning for software engineering and formal methods, on the Constructor Fabric project.

Constructor Fabric turns a company's informal knowledge into production software through a pipeline of composable capability units called gears: requirements → architecture → product fit → framework (G1) → application → runtime. We are building a World Model over that pipeline — a model that does not just generate code, but predicts the consequences of an architectural decision: total cost of ownership, unintended side effects, latency and failure behaviour, and whether a proposed composition is even admissible.


The central object is not a digital twin of the application but its formal architectural skeleton: gear contracts (GearSpec), a typed attributed hypergraph of the application (AppGraph), a composition algebra that defines which assemblies are legal, and several semantic projections (types, protocols, resources, security) over which properties are proved, refuted by counterexample, or reported as an explainable gap. All of it is written in a domain-specific language whose syntax trees and graphs we keep in a projectional editor (JetBrains MPS) — so the DSL is not a convenience layer, it is the thing that defines the model's state space and the boundary of what the model is allowed to propose.

What you will work on
Depending on your background, one or two of:

  1. Formal skeleton and composition — GearSpec as a contract $(Requires, Provides, State, Effects, Assumptions, Guarantees, Parameters)$; AppGraph as a typed attributed hypergraph; an algebra of assembly (sequential, parallel, feedback, refinement); semantic projections and system-level invariants over trajectories.
  2. Architecture synthesis as an inverse problem — given a specification, load and constraints, find the composition of gears that realises it. Constraint solving and MCTS as the baseline; a learned transition/value model for ranking and pruning; LLM proposals treated strictly as candidate hypotheses that a DSL parser, type checker and property checks must then admit or reject.
  3. DSL design and language engineering — the gear DSL and its glue layer decide which AppGraphs are expressible at all, and therefore where the search space ends. This thread covers the abstract syntax and static semantics of that DSL; the requirement that an architectural decision be unbypassable by construction (you must not be able to wire authentication around the Auth Resolver); what happens to the language when gear contracts change or a 201st gear is added; projectional representation of graphs with cycles; and the open hypothesis that a specialised G1-DSL is generated together with every G1.
  4. Local transition models and pipeline surrogates — fast approximate predictors for single pipeline steps (spec change → code quality, architecture → product fit, app → runtime outcome), with calibrated uncertainty, validated against real telemetry.
  5. Data — reconstructing (specification → architecture) pairs from open repositories at scale, plus synthetic project generation from a fixed gear set and DSL grammar to cover rare transitions, gaps and counterexamples.

Profile

  • MSc (or equivalent) in computer science, mathematics, or a mathematical natural science.
  • Coursework in compilers, programming-language theory, language design or model-driven engineering is a strong positive signal, half of this project is deciding what a formal architecture description is allowed to say.
  • Evidence that you finish things: a maintained open-source repository, a peer-reviewed publication, or a strong competition result.
  • Fluent technical English.
  • Most importantly: the habit of stating an assumption explicitly and designing an experiment that could falsify it.

Required mathematical background

Core skills:

  • Probability and statistics. Estimation, Bayesian inference, uncertainty quantification and calibration (proper scoring rules, reliability diagrams, ECE), experiment design and significance testing. A prediction we cannot calibrate is not usable here.
  • Linear algebra and multivariate calculus at the level needed to derive, not just call, a training objective: matrix calculus, gradients, stochastic optimisation, conditioning.
  • Discrete mathematics and graph theory. Typed and attributed graphs and hypergraphs, subgraph matching and isomorphism, graph rewriting, reachability, basic complexity classes.
  • Mathematical logic and formal methods. First-order logic, type systems, SAT/SMT, temporal logic (LTL/CTL) and model checking, pre/post-conditions, invariants, refinement.
  • Sequential decision making. MDP/POMDP, dynamic programming, model-based RL, latent state-space (world) models, Monte-Carlo Tree Search.

Strong command of at least one, working knowledge of a second:

  • Formal languages, semantics and language engineering — grammars (context-free, attribute and graph grammars), derivation and reachability, parsing; abstract versus concrete syntax; operational and denotational semantics; metamodelling, model-driven engineering, model-to-model transformation, and projectional (structural) editing of the kind JetBrains MPS implements. We are asking for the education, not the tool: you should know why a projectional editor exists, what a metamodel buys you over a text grammar, and how a language evolves without breaking its existing models. Hands-on MPS experience is explicitly not required — we will teach it.
  • Category theory for compositional systems — monoidal and traced monoidal categories, functors as semantic projections, string diagrams, operads. This is the language of our assembly algebra.
  • Causal inference — structural causal models, do-calculus, counterfactuals, identifiability. Required for the "what happens if we replace this technology / move on-premises" class of questions, which similarity search alone cannot answer.
  • Queueing theory and applied stochastic processes — M/M/1 and networks of queues, heavy tails, retries, timeouts, partial failure and reliability models. This is the resource and stochastic projection.
  • Combinatorial optimisation, constraint programming and program synthesis theory — CEGIS, version-space algebras, symmetry breaking, search heuristics.
  • Representation learning theory — VAEs and latent dynamics, GNN expressiveness (Weisfeiler-Leman hierarchy), permutation equivariance, embedding migration under a changing vocabulary.

Required hands-on programming skills

This is an engineering-heavy PhD. We expect code that another person can clone, run and reproduce — not notebooks that worked once.

Must have:

  • Python (professional level). Type hints, packaging, `pytest`, profiling, `asyncio`, memory-aware data structures. You write unbuffered, logged, restartable long-running jobs by default.
  • Training loops written from scratch, custom datasets and collation, mixed precision, multi-GPU; experiment tracking (W&B or MLflow), configuration management (Hydra), strict seed and artefact reproducibility.
  • Graph machine learning. PyTorch Geometric or DGL — message passing, heterogeneous and typed graphs, graph transformers, handling graphs whose node vocabulary changes between versions.
  • Solvers and verification tooling driven from Python. Z3 or cvc5 hands-on; demonstrated exposure to at least one model checker (TLA+/TLC, SPIN, NuSMV, Alloy) or proof assistant (Lean, Coq, Isabelle).
  • Code as data. AST manipulation, `tree-sitter`, static analysis, dependency and interface graph extraction, large-scale repository mining.
  • Parallel data pipelines. `multiprocessing`, Ray or Dask; checkpointing, heartbeats, cost estimation before launching a run that touches millions of files.
  • LLM engineering. API orchestration, structured and grammar-constrained decoding, evaluation harnesses, token/cost accounting — with the discipline to treat model output as a hypothesis subject to formal checks.
  • Linux, git, code review, shell.

Desirable:

  • Language tooling you have actually used: ANTLR, Xtext, Lark, or a parser, type checker or interpreter you wrote yourself. Our internal representation of gear syntax trees and graphs lives in JetBrains MPS — again, we do not ask for MPS experience, only that you are comfortable reading and extending a metamodel; Java/Kotlin literacy helps once you get there.
  • JAX, or compiler / SAT-SMT internals.
  • Infrastructure literacy — Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, OpenTelemetry/Prometheus — since the resource projection is calibrated against real deployment telemetry.
  • One systems language (Rust, Go or C++) for performance-critical search.
  • Prior experience with production software architecture, or with a brownfield system you had to change without breaking.

Funding

The appointment provides full financial coverage through a dedicated fellowship, comprising:

  • Monthly stipend of €1,650
  • Monthly research-cost allowance of €100 (Forschungskostenpauschale)
  • Health-insurance subsidy of €100 per month

Location: Bremen, Germany

Duration: 3 years, full time

Start date:  November 2026

Application package must include

  • CV, including publications, code, or research projects.
  • Cover letter (1–2 pages) explaining your motivation, research interests, and fit with the project.
  • A link to code you have written.
  • A one-page research statement picking one open research question from the project and sketching how you would approach it.
  • Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificate and transcripts.
  • Contact information for 2–3 academic referees.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interviews.

title: Lead Product Manager
description:
About us 

Constructor Labs is the research arm of Constructor Knowledge, based at Campus Ring 1 in Bremen, Germany. Our work is organized around three units: Knowledge Labs, Cyber Labs and Science Labs. We apply computing, software and robotics research to make scientists, teachers and students more effective, working with institutional partners that include CERN, NUS, Carnegie Mellon and Fraunhofer. 

Constructor Practice is the hands-on practice platform within the Constructor Technology learning suite, alongside Learn, Assess, Proctor, Schedule and Groups. It spans an unusually broad portfolio: curriculum-aligned virtual science labs; the evidence-based intervention products Calcularis (numeracy and dyscalculia), Grafari/Orthograph (literacy and dyslexia); and browser-based Software & IT and Coding labs for technical training. Shared capabilities include cloud-based hands-on environments with no installation, automated assessment and grading, group assignments and instructor assistance, LMS integration, and learner analytics and dashboards. 

The product is in production across three distinct markets. Higher education and research, schools and public education authorities, and corporate and vocational training. The platform operates under GDPR, FERPA, COPPA and SOPIPA commitments. 

About the Role

You will own Constructor Practice content portfolio of products (currently includes Practice: Science Labs and Practice: Schools Math and Literacy with future extension to other disciplines) end to end: strategy, roadmap, commercial performance and delivery. This is a lead product management position with full accountability for the product line rather than for a single feature area or squad. 

The scope is wider than a conventional PM role. You will sit in front of clients during presales, shape the go-to-market with sales and marketing, define the roadmap across a portfolio serving three different buyer types, and work with product owners and engineering to bring releases in on time and on budget. Where the product line needs something that has no owner, it is yours. 

Practice has an established customer base and a portfolio that has grown through acquisition and expansion into markets with little in common: a Swiss canton buying dyscalculia intervention for primary schools has almost nothing in common with Acronis training its partner ecosystem. Bringing coherence to that portfolio, deciding what to invest in, what to standardize and what to retire, is the central problem of this role. 

Reporting and scope 

  • Reports to: Head of SI and Edu, Constructor Labs. 
  • Level: Lead Product Manager. You will lead the product team including product owners, engineers and subject matter experts, with a view to building a larger product team as the line grows. 
  • Product surface: all Constructor Practice content products, namely Science Labs, Calcularis, Grafari/Orthograph, Software & IT and Coding, in cooperation with the shared platform layer covering assessment, analytics, LMS integration and deployment. 
  • Markets: higher education and research institutions, schools and public education authorities, and corporate and vocational training providers. 
  • Interfaces: engineering and product owners, presales and sales, marketing, customer success and support, Constructor Tech engineering and product teams, Nexademy content team, Constructor Labs research, and Constructor Labs Solutions as an integration channel. 

The role is both outward and inward facing. You are expected to be in client conversations and in sprint reviews in the same week, and to carry what you learn in one into the other. 

Duties & Responsibilities:

Product strategy. Set the direction for Practice across its three markets: where to invest, where to standardize on shared platform capability, and where a module should be sustained rather than developed. Maintain a defensible view of the competitive position against virtual lab providers, intervention software and hands-on technical training platforms. 

Roadmap and prioritization. Own a published roadmap with a clear rationale for sequencing, balancing client commitments, platform debt, regulatory requirements and new capability. Say no in a way that holds up, and keep the roadmap current as commitments change. 

Discovery and requirements. Work directly with teachers, learning designers, lab administrators, IT staff and corporate training leads to establish what the product needs to do. Translate that into specifications, acceptance criteria and measurable outcomes rather than feature lists. 

Delivery with engineering. Work with product owners and development teams through planning, sprint reviews and release. Hold scope, schedule and budget together, escalate early when one of the three has to give, and make the trade-off explicit rather than absorbing it quietly. 

Presales support. Act as the product authority in qualified opportunities: demonstrations, solution design, technical objection handling, RFP and tender responses, security and compliance questionnaires. Judge which client-specific requests are viable and which are not. 

Go-to-market. Own positioning, messaging and the launch plan for each release and module, working with marketing and sales enablement. Produce the materials that let the sales team sell Practice without you in the room. 

Client relationships. Run a regular cadence with reference and strategic accounts, gather structured feedback, manage expectations on committed features and turn successful deployments into case studies and references. 

Pricing and commercials. Own the pricing and packaging model across modules and market segments, with input on licensing, bundling within the Constructor learning suite, and the commercial terms of custom work. 

Compliance and trust. Keep the product aligned with GDPR, FERPA, COPPA and SOPIPA obligations and with accessibility requirements, working with legal and security. Child-facing products in public education carry a higher bar, and meeting it is part of the roadmap. 

Performance measurement. Instrument the product, track adoption, engagement and learning outcomes, and use the evidence to decide what to build next and what to stop. 

Qualifications & Experience:

Product ownership at scale. Five or more years in product management, including at least three owning a B2B SaaS product line with revenue accountability rather than a single feature area. 

Education or adjacent domain. Experience with EdTech, assessment, e-learning, corporate L&D tooling or another domain where the buyer, the administrator and the end user are three different people with different measures of success. 

Delivery discipline. A track record of shipping on committed dates and budgets with agile teams, working through product owners and engineering leads, and managing the scope conversations that make that possible. 

Commercial fluency. Comfort in front of clients and in presales, with the ability to run a demonstration, defend a roadmap position and contribute to pricing and packaging decisions. 

Technical credibility. Enough depth in cloud platforms, LMS integration standards such as LTI and SCORM, APIs and analytics to hold your own with engineering and with a client's IT team, without needing to write the code yourself. 

Evidence-based decisions. Fluency with product analytics and experimentation, and the judgement to distinguish a signal worth acting on from a loud customer. 

Portfolio judgement. Experience managing several products or modules at once, and a willingness to make and defend investment and retirement decisions. 

Languages. Business-fluent English. German is a bonus, given the Swiss, German and Austrian school and public-sector customer base. 

Communication. Written and verbal clarity with audiences ranging from a primary school teacher to a university CIO to a development team. 

Nice to have 

  • Experience with virtual labs, simulation environments or browser-based development and IT training environments. 
  • Background in special educational needs, learning intervention or evidence-based pedagogy, particularly dyscalculia or dyslexia support. 
  • Familiarity with public-sector education procurement in DACH, including cantonal and Länder-level buying. 
  • Experience with student data privacy regimes (GDPR in an education context, FERPA, COPPA, SOPIPA) and WCAG accessibility conformance. 
  • Prior work in a group structure where a product is sold both directly and through an integration or services channel. 
  • A background in teaching, instructional design or learning science. 

What we offer 

  • A product line with an established base, in production with universities, public education authorities and corporate academies across Europe and beyond. 
  • Genuine end-to-end ownership, from strategy and pricing through to release, without the role being split across a commercial owner and a delivery owner. 
  • Access to our researchers, including principal investigators and education methodologists from Constructor Labs, and the ability to route applied research questions into the Labs. 
  • Salary and annual bonus tied to the product line's commercial and delivery targets. The band is competitive for a lead product role in DACH or the UK and depends on location and experience. 
  • A distribution channel beyond direct sales, through Constructor Labs Solutions and the partner network.

Qualifications

  • Ability to leverage managed solutions (Vertex AI) while knowing how to "dive into code" to debug distributed architectures, develop custom connectors, and bypass framework limitations.
  • Demonstrated ability to evolve in shifting technical environments.
  • Operational skills on GCP and understanding of containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) to autonomously deploy the Agentic layer.

Technical Environment

  • Agent orchestration: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Vertex AI Agent Builder
  • Infrastructure & Cloud: GCP (Google Cloud Platform), Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines.
  • AI & Integration Protocols: Model Context Protocol (MCP), LLMs (Gemini), LLM routing & memory management.
  • Security & Access: Google Cloud Model Armor.
  • Execution Engine: Databricks, AWS EKS, Sagemaker
  • Payload: Python, Spark, Scikit-Learn, Tensorflow / Pytorch, Pyspark

  • Orchestration:  Airflow

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!

Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.

This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.

Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly’s operational and analytical systems.

This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data.

What you will do

  • Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.
  • Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.
  • Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.
  • Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products.
  • Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution.
  • Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery.
  • Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes.
  • Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations.

What we are looking for

  • Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes.
  • Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, transactions, replication, or operational performance.
  • Experience with Kafka, event streaming, CDC, Debezium, or adjacent data-movement technologies. Direct Debezium experience is valuable, but strong fundamentals matter more.
  • Experience building software that other engineers use: CLIs, internal platforms, control planes, automation, CI validation, developer tooling, or self-service workflows.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud or infrastructure platforms, including runtime isolation, deployment, observability, and operational ownership.
  • Ability to turn ambiguous architectural direction into practical increments, make trade-offs explicit, and deliver useful production systems without waiting for perfect certainty.
  • Clear written and spoken communication in English. This role involves aligning multiple engineering teams around standards, contracts, and ownership boundaries.

Useful experience, but not required

  • DataHub or other data catalog, lineage, or governance systems.
  • Open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, object-store-backed data lakes, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse, or analytical storage systems.
  • GitHub Actions, policy-as-code, infrastructure-as-code, controllers, operators, or reconciliation-based systems.
  • Data contracts, schema registries, Protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema, compatibility checking, field-level metadata, or contract testing.
  • Experience supporting analytics, AI/ML, feature-store-style access patterns, or cross-domain product-service integrations.
  • Experience with JVM languages and Python, TypeScript, Go, or Ruby.

What we offer you

At Smartly, we offer a place where you can do meaningful technical work while growing with a global team.

  • Inclusive global culture built on trust, transparency, open feedback, and respect for different perspectives.
  • Global impact through technology used by major brands to plan, create, optimize, and understand digital advertising at scale.
  • Wellbeing support, paid holidays, family leave, and sustainable ways of working.
  • Equity options, performance-based rewards, competitive compensation, and career development opportunities.
  • A flexible hybrid workplace that balances office collaboration with focused remote work. At Smartly we work 3 days a week from the office.

About Smartly

Smartly is an advertising technology company helping brands create, manage, optimize, and understand digital advertising across major media platforms. Our engineering organization builds the systems that connect media, creative, and intelligence capabilities into a product used by customers globally.

We value clear communication, ownership, curiosity, and collaboration across teams. We want Smartly to be a place where people can do strong work, grow, and feel respected.

Not sure you tick every box? Please apply anyway. We care about strong engineering fundamentals, ownership, curiosity, and the ability to build reliable systems with others. Direct experience with every technology listed here is less important than the judgment to learn, reason from first principles, and ship useful platform capabilities.

About Smartly

Smartly is the AI-powered advertising technology company transforming ad experiences for brands and their consumers. Our comprehensive advertising platform seamlessly integrates the capabilities of media, creative, and intelligence to power more than 800 billion impressions and generate more than 300 billion creatives annually, delivering tangible business outcomes for brands and advertisers.

Smartly is the only company in the industry recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: Creative Advertising Technologies with PwC validating the results it delivers for brands. We manage creative and media for 700+ brands worldwide and $6B in ad spend across the largest media platforms, including Facebook, Google, Instagram, Pinterest, Snap, and TikTok. Our end-to-end technology, unmatched access to media platforms and exceptional customer service help Fortune 500 brands to reach and engage consumers and learn what performs best.Smartly is a multinational and diverse team of 750+ Smartlies from 60+ nationalities, working in 13 countries. Together, we want to create and maintain an inclusive environment where everyone feels respected and heard. Our Diversity, Equity & Inclusion approach is at the heart of it.

Visit Smartly to learn more.

raw.description:
About Heidi Systems

Heidi Systems builds the energy OS for real estate. We help property managers and owners get their heating, water and electricity meters online, see consumption in real time and run the yearly utility billing without paper, Excel and site visits.

Submetering in Germany is still mostly analog. Meters get read by hand, data sits in PDFs, and tenants see their consumption once a year. We change that end to end: we install the meters and gateways in the building, collect the data and build the web platform property managers work in.

We're a small team in Berlin. Product and engineering work directly with the founders, and what you ship lands with real customers fast.

The role

We're looking for a best-in-class frontend engineer. Someone whose code other engineers learn from.

You'll be our senior frontend engineer and own the web platform end to end: architecture, code quality and the day-to-day experience of the property managers using it.

The platform is a SvelteKit and TypeScript app. It shows consumption data per building and unit, flags anomalies, manages tenants and owners, and produces the documents for the yearly billing. A lot of it is data-heavy UI, and it has to be right, because the numbers end up on invoices.

You'll work closely with our backend engineers and the founders, and you'll help onboard and mentor junior developers and interns as the team grows.

What you'll do

  • Own the frontend architecture of our SvelteKit app: routing, load functions, SSR, state and how we talk to the backend via oRPC

  • Ship features end to end, from a rough idea with the founders to production, often before the design is final

  • Build the data-heavy parts of the product: consumption dashboards, notification rules, tenant and owner management, billing documents

  • Set up and maintain our component library on Tailwind and DaisyUI so the UI stays consistent as we add features

  • Raise the bar on quality: strict TypeScript, Vitest coverage, code reviews, a sane PR flow

  • Shape the API contract together with backend (types, Zod schemas, error handling) so frontend and backend stay in sync

  • Mentor juniors and interns through reviews and pairing

What you bring

  • 5+ years of professional frontend experience, ideally at startups or other fast-moving product teams

  • 2+ years building production apps with Svelte and SvelteKit, with a deep understanding of its reactivity model, stores, lifecycle, routing, load functions and SSR

  • Strong TypeScript: strict mode, generics, utility types, and the judgment to know when types help and when they get in the way

  • Hands-on with Tailwind CSS (DaisyUI is a plus)

  • Experience with RPC-style APIs (oRPC, tRPC or similar) and typed contracts between frontend and backend

  • Testing as a habit: Vitest, JSDom or comparable tooling

  • Comfortable in a Unix environment (Linux or macOS), with Git, branches and PRs

  • You've made architecture decisions on a real product and can explain the trade-offs

  • You work well with little oversight and ship in small, frequent steps

  • Fluent English, written and spoken

  • You're in Berlin or willing to move, and you're in our office 2 to 3 days a week

How we work

  • Hybrid in Berlin. You're in the office 2 to 3 days a week. That's fixed. The rest of the week you work from wherever you like.

  • Short paths. You talk to the founders directly, most decisions take one call.

  • Real ownership. The frontend is yours to shape, and you'll set many of the standards the team builds on.

  • Real impact. Your work runs in buildings across Germany and makes energy use visible where people live.

  • Room to grow with the company as the engineering team gets bigger.

Your next steps

If you match most of these requirements and are ready to help digitize the building sector, we encourage you to apply. You will join a growing team where your work directly shapes the future of energy management in real estate.

MSW ist eine mittelständische Wirtschaftsprüfungs- und Steuerberatungsgesellschaft mit Sitz in Stuttgart am Pragsattel. Mit rund 20 Mitarbeitenden sind wir groß genug für abwechslungsreiche Mandate und klare Entwicklungsperspektiven und gleichzeitig klein genug für ein persönliches, kollegiales Miteinander.

Bei MSW gestalten wir unsere Arbeit bewusst anders: Wir legen Wert auf qualitativ hochwertige Beratung, langfristige Mandatsbeziehungen und eine individuelle Betreuung. Unsere Philosophie: „Der Erfolg unserer Mandanten ist auch unser eigener Erfolg.“ Wir verstehen uns als verlässlicher Partner und Coach, der jederzeit zur Seite steht, wenn Unterstützung benötigt wird. Diese Haltung spiegelt sich auch in unserer Teamkultur wider. So fragen sich neue Teammitglieder nach kurzer Zeit oft: „Warum habe ich nicht früher den Arbeitgeber gewechselt?“ Wir nennen das den MSW-Effekt.

Neugierig geworden? Dann lerne uns und den MSW-Effekt kennen.

Aufgaben

Gestalten statt abarbeiten – Der MSW-Effekt.

Als Prüfungsassistent bist du bei uns von Anfang an Teil des Mandats und arbeitest eng mit unseren Wirtschaftsprüfern zusammen. Du lernst die Unternehmen hinter den Zahlen kennen, übernimmst Schritt für Schritt eigene Prüffelder und wirst dabei fachlich begleitet, statt ins kalte Wasser geworfen zu werden. Getreu dem Motto „eigenständig, aber nie allein“ wächst dein Aufgabenbereich mit deiner Erfahrung:

  • Mitwirkung bei Jahres- und Konzernabschlussprüfungen
  • Eigenverantwortliche Bearbeitung einzelner Prüffelder nach Einarbeitung
  • Prüfung von Buchhaltungen, Belegen und Einzelpositionen
  • Unterstützung bei der Erstellung von Prüfungsberichten
  • Mitarbeit bei prüfungsnahen und betriebswirtschaftlichen Fragestellungen
  • Mitwirkung an der weiteren Digitalisierung unserer Prüfungsprozesse

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit.

Ob frisch von der Hochschule oder mit ersten Berufsjahren im Gepäck, bei uns zählt, dass du mitdenkst und dich entwickeln willst. Klare Strukturen, ein überschaubares Mandantenportfolio und echte Teamarbeit sorgen dafür, dass du schnell hineinwächst.

Idealerweise bringst du mit:

  • Abgeschlossenes wirtschaftswissenschaftliches Studium, idealerweise mit Schwerpunkt Wirtschaftsprüfung, Rechnungswesen oder Steuern
  • Erste praktische Erfahrung durch Praktika oder eine Werkstudententätigkeit ist willkommen, aber kein Muss
  • Interesse an einer langfristigen Entwicklung in der Wirtschaftsprüfung
  • Selbstständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise
  • Verlässlichkeit und hohe fachliche Sorgfalt
  • Wohnort in Stuttgart oder gut erreichbarer Umgebung

Benefits

Unser Angebot an dich. Dein MSW-Effekt.

Wir bieten dir die optimalen Rahmenbedingungen für deine Entwicklung.

Dazu gehören:

  • Homeoffice: Bis zu 3 Tage, je nach deiner persönlichen Lebenssituation.
  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Plane deine Arbeitstage flexibel, um Beruf und Privatleben optimal zu vereinbaren.
  • Team & Kultur: Bei MSW zählt das wir. Hier findest du ein kollegiales Umfeld, überschaubare Teams sowie gegenseitige Unterstützung und Wertschätzung. Unser 4-beiniger “Feel-Good-Manager" sorgt täglich für gute Laune und Kuscheleinheiten.
  • Moderne Arbeitsumgebung: Moderne Räumlichkeiten, ergonomische Arbeitsplätze, mehrere Bildschirme und digitale Tools sorgen für angenehmes Arbeiten.
  • Business-Bike: Wir unterstützen deine nachhaltige Mobilität und bieten dir ein Business-Bike an.
  • Ideale Lage: Zentrale Lage in Stuttgart am Pragsattel.
  • Parkplätze: Direkt am Büro vorhanden. Damit ist stressfreies Ankommen garantiert.

Dein Weg zu uns.

Wenn dir gefällt, was du liest, sollten wir uns kennenlernen. Bitte sende uns deinen Lebenslauf zu. Ein Anschreiben ist optional. Gerne beantworten wir auch vorab deine Fragen. Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

MSW GmbH & Co. KG WPG, StBG

Maybachstraße 50, 70469 Stuttgart

0711-342478-0

Du bindest Produkttexte und Bilder in Abstimmung mit Content & Design ein. Du prüfst Artikel anhand unserer Checklisten und bereitest sie für die Freigabe vor. Du kontrollierst nach der Veröffentlichung, ob Informationen und Darstellung im Shop stimmen, und unterstützt die Übergabe an unser Marktplatzteam. Du prüfst Seiten und Funktionen auf dem Smartphone und am Desktop. Du dokumentierst Fehler und schlägst Verbesserungen für Navigation, Produktauswahl und Serviceinformationen vor. Du unterstützt bei der Pflege und beim Testen unseres Produktfinders und weiterer digitaler Services. Du bereitest Anforderungen für unsere Digitalagentur YipYips vor und prüfst umgesetzte Änderungen gemeinsam mit dem Team. Auch andere Studienrichtungen passen, wenn du entsprechendes Interesse und praktische Fähigkeiten mitbringst. Du interessierst dich dafür, wie Menschen Produkte suchen, Informationen verstehen und online bestellen. Du kannst auf Deutsch sicher mit Produktinformationen arbeiten und Fehler oder Verbesserungsvorschläge verständlich beschreiben. Das erwartet dich Praktische Einblicke in den gesamten Weg vom Produktdatensatz bis zum verkaufsfertigen Artikel. Einblicke in Shopoptimierung und die Zusammenarbeit mit einer Digitalagentur. Eigene, überschaubare Aufgabenpakete und die Möglichkeit, schrittweise mehr Verantwortung zu übernehmen. Ein tolle Arbeitsumgebung durch ein wertschätzendes Team, das dich fördert und ein Büro im Loft-Stil Du arbeitest bei uns vor Ort in Aachen . Our CSAs will serve as trusted advisors, leveraging their deep understanding of DevSecOps best practices, industry trends and our software capabilities to help customers navigate complex challenges and achieve their desired outcomes.

title: Technical Lead (m/f/d), Robotics & AI Software
description:
About the role :

At the heart of our offering is a versatile software platform for orchestrating complex robotic systems, from industrial robot arms and mobile manipulators to humanoids. We bring it into real production environments with international customers and delivery partners, often in applications nobody has automated before.

As Technical Lead, you are one of the people we turn to when it matters most. When a critical project hits a wall, whether the problem is technical, organizational, or both, you step in, get to the root of it, and get it back on track. You work at the staff level alongside product and project management, and your judgment shapes what we build: which problems the platform solves next, how projects are scoped, and where the technical boundaries lie.

Your Responsibilities :

  • Take technical ownership of our most critical customer projects and turn around those that are off track.
  • Diagnose problems across the whole system: robot hardware, controls, perception, AI models, software, and integration.
  • Make the call on technical direction when there is no obvious answer, and stand behind it with customers, partners, and management.
  • Step into project leadership where needed: re-plan scope, reset expectations, and get the team moving again.
  • Shape the product roadmap with what you learn in the field, and turn one-off solutions into platform capabilities.
  • Challenge and sharpen the project scope early, before commitments are made, together with Sales, Pre-Sales, and project management.
  • Act as a technical counterpart for senior customer and partner stakeholders.
  • Coach engineers across teams, and raise the technical bar by example.

Essential Skills

  • Master's degree or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Mechatronics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, or a comparable field.
  • 8+ years of hands-on experience in robotics, gained in a startup, a research institute, or a comparable environment where you had to cover a broad range of topics yourself.
  • Deep technical knowledge across several of these: motion planning and control, perception and computer vision, robot learning or AI models, real-time and embedded systems, and software architecture.
  • A track record of solving hard problems in real deployments, not just in the lab.
  • Confident in taking on project management responsibility when the situation calls for it.
  • Clear communicator who can explain complex technical situations to engineers, customers, and management alike.

Beneficial Skills

  • Fluent German; Mandarin is a plus.
  • Experience with humanoids, mobile manipulation, or Vision-Language-Action models.

What we offer

  • A dynamic high-tech company, combined with financial soundness and world-class investors.

Agile Robots SE is an international high-tech company based in Munich, Germany with a production site in Kaufbeuren and more than 3500 employees worldwide. Our mission is to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and robotics by developing systems that combine state-of-the-art force-moment-sensing and world-leading image-processing technology. This unique combination of technologies allows us to provide user-friendly and affordable robotic solutions that enable intelligent precision assembly.

description:
The AI Teams at Agile Robots are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer (m/f/d) Computer Vision for Robotics, who will design and train deep-learning models for visual servoing in precision robot manipulation. Your model's output steers the robot as it moves, so inference latency and sub-millimetre accuracy both decide whether the task succeeds.

Responsibilities

  • Method Development: Develop deep-learning methods for visual servoing and robotic vision, adapting and combining existing methods for new tasks where that requires significant changes.
  • Model Training: Design, train, fine-tune, and evaluate models in PyTorch, including adapting pretrained and foundation models to real robot tasks.
  • Perception Methods: Develop 2D and 3D perception for pose estimation, depth, tracking, and geometric understanding, combining learned, classical, and optimization-based methods where each fits.
  • Closed-Loop Integration: Integrate learned models into closed-loop robot control for high-precision manipulation.
  • Robot Evaluation: Evaluate models on real robots and precision manipulation tasks, analyse failure cases, and improve robustness and generalization.
  • Real-Time Deployment: Build real-time inference pipelines in C++ and Python and optimize models with ONNX, TensorRT, and CUDA to meet the timing of the control loop.

Essential Skills

  • Background: Master's degree or PhD in computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of research and industry experience, with three or more years in machine learning, computer vision, or robotics.
  • ML Pipeline: Hands-on experience designing, training, and tuning deep-learning models end to end in PyTorch.
  • Method Development: Experience adapting, combining, or extending existing machine learning or vision methods for a new task, with changes that required understanding how those methods work internally.
  • Computer Vision: Solid understanding of computer vision and 2D/3D geometry.
  • Programming: Software development in Python, with working knowledge of C++.

Beneficial Skills

  • Robot Control: Understanding of robot kinematics, feedback control, or visual servoing, or experience with high-precision manipulation. The team supports candidates in building this experience on the job.
  • Model Deployment: Experience deploying optimized models with ONNX, TensorRT, or comparable frameworks, including on embedded or industrial GPU platforms.

  • Industrial Cameras: Experience with industrial 2D/3D cameras, lens models, camera calibration, or point clouds.

About the Position:

We are looking for a Security Engineer to support, automate and continuously improve the secure configuration of our enterprise assets. In this role, you will be the central point of contact for hardening standards, access controls, and the protection of our IT infrastructure against common attack vectors. You will work closely with various teams and locations to implement security requirements in a practical and sustainable way.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Configuration Standards: Develop, maintain, and harden the security configuration standards for end-user devices, servers, network components, and software (on-prem/SAAS) 
  • Identity and Access Management: Manage and oversee centralized Identity and Access Management throughout the account and employee lifecycles, including account provisioning, modification, and deprovisioning during onboarding, role changes, and onboarding
  • Compliance Monitoring & Audits: Conduct recurring control reviews to verify that approved security processes, technical specifications, configurations, account management practices, and access controls are implemented and operating effectively across the organization
  • Security Automation: Automate configuration validation and remediation, and integrate security-baseline checks into infrastructure provisioning and deployment workflows
  • Collaboration: Work closely with various teams and locations to implement and oversee the above security measures in practice

Your Profile:

  • 5+ years of expertise in IT security with relevant exposure to configuration and hardening
  • 2+ years of practical experience implementing security frameworks and standards, such as CIS Controls and Benchmarks, NIST guidance, and ISO/IEC 27001
  • Solid knowledge and practical experience of hardening operating systems (Windows/Linux/Mac) and network components
  • 3+ years of experience with Identity & Access Management concepts (roles, permissions, recertification) Page 2 of 3
  • Familiarity with configuration management or compliance tools 
  • Analytical and strategic thinking
  • Independent working style and initiative
  • Strong communication skills
  • Fluent English and German would be beneficial

Beneficial skills:

  • Scripting skills (Python, PowerShell, or Bash)
  • Knowledge with endpoint protection platforms (EDR/XDR)
  • Security Monitoring, Investigation, and Threat Detection
  • Experience integrating automated configuration, hardening, and compliance checks into infrastructure provisioning and deployment pipelines
  • Any Relevant Certifications

What we offer

  • A dynamic high-tech company, combined with financial soundness and world-class investors.
  • Join an interdisciplinary, international team with 60+ different nationalities in a collaborative work environment.
  • Lots of development opportunities as we continue to grow.
  • Challenging tasks and impactful projects alongside experts that enable professional and personal growth.
  • Corporate Benefits Program covering health, mobility, and learning for 100€ net per month.
  • Modern office facilities with a rooftop terrace overlooking Munich, free drinks & fruits, and regular company events contribute to a good working environment

About us

Agile Robots SE is an international high-tech company based in Munich, Germany with a production site in Kaufbeuren and more than 3500 employees worldwide. Our mission is to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and robotics by developing systems that combine state-of-the-art force-moment-sensing and world-leading image-processing technology. This unique combination of technologies allows us to provide user-friendly and affordable robotic solutions that enable intelligent precision assembly. 

This is made possible by our employees, who bring out the best in each and every day with creativity and enthusiasm. Become part of this team and shape the future of robotics with us!

We are proud of our diversity and welcome your application regardless of gender and sexual identity, nationality, ethnicity, religion, age, or disability.

title: DevOps Engineer with AI/ML Evaluation Focus
description:
About the Position:

We are looking for an experienced, motivated mid-level professional for a dual role: classic IT DevOps responsibilities combined with the evaluation and support of AI/ML models and vendors. This position is a great fit for someone who wants to combine technical infrastructure expertise with an interest in current AI/ML developments. The role sits in internal IT and is not part of robotics product development. The two areas are not equally plannable: production operations take precedence, and AI/ML evaluation runs as project work around operational load.

Responsibilities :

  • CI/CD, Automation & Software Development: Build, maintain, and improve CI/CD pipelines using GitLab CI and Jenkins; automate recurring operational processes; collaborate with development teams on deployment processes; develop small-scale internal software for IT and other internal departments; support software integrations, particularly Entra ID, Active Directory, and SSO.
  • Cloud, Infrastructure & Operations: Manage and optimize AWS, Azure, and GCP infrastructure; use Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible), Docker and Kubernetes on select projects (not a global standard); operate the largely Linux-based landscape (approx. 80–85% Ubuntu), including patch/update management; ensure availability, scalability, security, monitoring, logging and alerting (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK); manage backup/disaster recovery and cloud cost optimization.
  • Production Support & AI/ML Evaluation: Manage incidents and troubleshoot production environments (no on-call rota currently planned; if introduced, it will be agreed and compensated separately); evaluate AI/ML models and vendors (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft Azure AI) for performance, cost, suitability, cost-benefit, and licensing; evaluate open-weight/self-hosted models (e.g. vLLM, Ollama) where data residency, data protection, or cost requirements make external APIs unsuitable.

  • AI Governance, Compliance & Enablement: Document model best practices, limitations, and use cases; track market developments; collaborate with business departments to identify new use cases; support compliance on data protection, security, and AI regulations, particularly the EU AI Act and GDPR (internal deployer-side use, not product conformity); train and enable internal staff on AI/ML tools, contributing to AI literacy under Art. 4 of the EU AI Act and internal AI governance/use guidelines

Your Profile:

  • Completed degree in Computer Science, IT, or comparable professional experience
  • 2 to 4 years of experience in a DevOps environment
  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD tooling; both GitLab CI and Jenkins are in use
  • Experience with at least one major public cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP); all three are in use
  • Solid experience operating Linux systems (Ubuntu), as the large majority of systems run on it
  • Experience with containerization (Docker); Kubernetes knowledge is a plus, as it is used on a per-project basis
  • Solid working knowledge of the core DevOps toolchain: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible), scripting (Python, Bash), and monitoring, logging, and alerting (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack)

  • Strong communication skills for collaborating with technical and non-technical teams

  • Lots of development opportunities as we continue to grow.
  • Challenging tasks and impactful projects alongside experts that enable professional and personal growth.
  • Corporate Benefits Program covering health, mobility, and learning for 100€ net per month.
  • Modern office facilities with a rooftop terrace overlooking Munich, free drinks & fruits, and regular company events contribute to a good working environment
